computation_or_rationale: Judgment about an uncertain outcome = subjectivity + uncertainty inherent risk factors (AU-C 315 SAS 145). Others lower or do not affect IR.
IR factors: complexity, subjectivity, change, uncertainty, susceptibility to management bias/fraud. Control effectiveness is control risk, not an IR factor.
Management integrity concern is pervasive -> FS-level RMM requiring overall responses (AU-C 315/330.05). Not limited to revenue; not cured by testing controls.
SAS 145 definition: significant risk = IR assessed close to the upper end of the spectrum (or treated as significant by another AU-C). Not tied to performance materiality or balance size.
AU-C 315 (SAS 145): if no plan to test OE of controls, CR assessed so RMM = IR (i.e., maximum).
Performance-based compensation = incentive/pressure (fraud risk factor; susceptibility to management bias).
Change IR factor = events/conditions changing over time, e.g., new accounting standard, new IT system.

Stand-back (AU-C 315.36): evaluate whether determination remains appropriate; substantive procedures for material items (AU-C 330.18) - wording of 330.18 under SAS 145 to verify (each relevant assertion of significant classes vs each material class).
Overall responses: assign more experienced staff, more supervision, emphasize skepticism, unpredictability, general changes in NTE. Others are assertion-level procedures.
Level 3 internally modeled valuation: high subjectivity, uncertainty, complexity, susceptibility to bias -> upper end.
Petty cash count sheet tells nothing about industry/regulatory environment.
Major customer distress -> collectibility (valuation/allowance of receivables, CECL) and possibly going concern given 45% concentration.
SAS 145 requires separate IR and CR assessments at the relevant assertion level.
Elastic (|E|=2>1): +5% price -> about -10% quantity; revenue factor 1.05 x 0.90 = 0.945, about -5.5%. Revenue falls.

Building permits = leading (Conference Board LEI). Unemployment rate commonly classed as lagging (LEI lagging index uses duration of unemployment); industrial production coincident; prime rate lagging.
SOX 302: CEO and CFO (principal executive and financial officers) certify each 10-Q/10-K incl. disclosure controls.
New product, no sales history, large build-up -> NRV/obsolescence -> inventory valuation.
Rapid tech change -> obsolescence of inventory (valuation).
Risk assessment procedures: inquiry, analytical procedures, observation and inspection (AU-C 315).
For significant risks the auditor identifies controls that address the risk and evaluates design and determines implementation (AU-C 315 SAS 145 26(a)(i), 26(d)).
Auditor must understand the entity's selection/application of accounting policies including changes and reasons (AU-C 315).
Not all business risks give rise to RMM; auditor considers only those that may result in RMM.
If no/ad hoc risk assessment process, auditor discusses with management and evaluates whether absence is appropriate or represents a deficiency (possibly SD/MW). Best available option; stem is thin.
Risk assessment procedures include inquiry and analytical procedures (plus observation and inspection). Near-duplicate of ue-16.
Engagement team discussion: susceptibility of FS to material misstatement incl. fraud (AU-C 315, 240).
Understanding relevant controls = evaluate design and determine implementation (not OE).
New ERP mid-year -> change factor, conversion risk, IT controls -> raises RMM.
Declining industry + heavy leverage -> going concern, covenant compliance, impairment.
AU-C 315: if auditor finds RMM management's process missed, evaluate whether process deficiency (possibly SD/MW).
Walkthrough shows control not in place -> not implemented -> cannot rely; deficiency; cannot test OE of nonexistent control.
Uncertainty factor = measurement depends on future events/unobservable inputs (estimates). (a) complexity, (b) change, (d) susceptibility to bias.
Lack of management competence in financial reporting is pervasive (control environment) -> FS level.
Regulator correspondence and in-house counsel best inform regulatory environment.
Control effectiveness is not an IR factor (relates to control risk).
Confirming A/R is a substantive (further) procedure, not a risk assessment procedure.
Discussion covers susceptibility to material misstatement incl. how fraud might occur; required every audit; key members, not management.
